lawyer:
Md Mahbub Ali, Advocate ------ For the Petitioners. 
None appears --------- For the Opposite-Parties.
parties:
Shah Ali and others -------- Petitioners
vs
Md Moniruddin Majumder and others ------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
On an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, this Rule was issued at the instance of the petitioners calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment dated 184-1996 and decree dated 23-4-1996 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Moulvibazar, in Title Appeal No. 121 of 1993 reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-10-1993 passed by the Assistant Judge, Kamalgonj in Title Suit No. 46 of 1991 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/ or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the predecessor of the opposite party Nos. 1-8, Moniruddin Majumder as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 46 of 1991 in the court of Assistant Judge, Kamalgonj, Moulvibazar, against the petitioners as defendant for recovery of possession stating, inter alia, that the schedule-1 land was sold to the plaintiff by defendant No. 1 by a registered sale deed dated 17-5-1983. After purchase the plaintiff constructed a tin shed house on the property and have been residing there with his family. Thereafter, Amena Khatun wife of the plaintiff purchased 8 sataks of land from plot No. 1362 adjacent south to the schedule-1 land by sale deed dated 25-11-1987. The plaintiff constructed a four storied building on the property purchased by him and his wife and now living therein. Again by a sale deed Amena Khatun purchased 15 sataks of land from south portion of plot No. 1362. In the aforesaid way the plaintiff and his wife purchased in total 49 sataks of land from plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. The said land is situated in a compact block wherein the plaintiff planted various trees and installed tube well. While the plaintiff in possession and enjoyment of the property since purchase, the defendant No.1 requested the plaintiff in the last part of Falgoon 1396 BS to allow him to stay in the suit house for the time being to enable him to construct his house on the adjacent land to the plaintiff's land. The plaintiff on candid allowed the defendant No: 1 considering his distress condition to stay in the suit house on the assurance that he will vacate and surrender possession of the suit house when asked by the plaintiff. But the defendant No. 1 on various pretext and pleas continued to live in the house for several months. Finding no way out the plaintiff in the midst of Baishakh 1397 BS finally asked the defendant No. 1 to vacate the house and handover vacant possession of the same to the plaintiff.

3. The defendant No. 1 assured the plaintiff that he will vacate the house very soon and handover vacant possession to the plaintiff. The defendant also disclosed that he sold the property in plot No. 1363 to the defendant No. 2. Meanwhile, taking advantage of defendant No. l's possession in the schedule-2 land the defendant No. 2 with the help of other threatened the plaintiff with dispossession form the north part of the suit land on 23rd Jaistha 1398. For the reason, the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 for a decree of permanent injunction against the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 along with others and in that suit got the suit land inspected through court by an Advocate Commissioner. Learned Advocate Commissioner found that the defendant No. 2 constructed a tin shed house measuring 8 x 7 hands just adjacent to south-east corner of the plaintiff's suit house. In the meantime, taking advantage of possessing the suit house by the defendant No. 1 as permissive possessor the defendant No. 2 dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land.

4. In the situation the plaintiff has withdrawn Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 with permission to sue a fresh and filed the instant suit for recovery of possession. It is also stated that the defendant No. 1 filed a criminal case against the plaintiffs and his son being No. 221 of 1991 under sections 107/114/117(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure which was ultimately rejected. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 most illegally dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land claiming that they have title in the suit property by purchase and dispossessed the plaintiff by constructing a tin shed house on the south-east corner of the suit land.

5. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable without a suit for partition and also denied that they dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit land on the date stated in the plaint or any other date. The case of the defendants are that plot No. 1362 measuring 44 sataks and plot No. 1363 measuring 35 sataks under khatian No. 99 are the suit land. The defendant No. 1 purchased in total 50 sataks of land from plot Nos. 1362 and 1363 from different persons and has been in possession of the same by constructing house and living therein with their family. While Ekhlas Mia the defendant No. 1 in possession he transferred 26 sataks of land to the plaintiff from plot No. 1362 by sale deed dated 17-5-1983 out of 57 sataks. After sale he remains in possession of 31 sataks land wherein his homestead and other establishment exists. The defendant No. 1 by sale deeds dated 1-6-1991 and 3-6-1991 transferred the said 31 sataks land to the defendant No. 2 and delivered possession of the same.

6. It is also stated that the defendant No. 1 never possessed the suit land as permissive possessor under the plaintiff and the plaintiff in the earlier Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 filed against the defendant did not claim that the suit property has been possessing by the defendant No. 1 as permissive possessor. But for the purpose of filing of the present suit against the defendants the plaintiff very cunningly made out a case that the defendant No.1 has been possessing the suit land as permissive possessor with the permission of the plaintiff. As such, the suit is a false one and liable to be dismissed.

7. The trial court framed four issues for determination of the dispute. In course of trial the plaintiff examined four witnesses including himself and submitted some documents which was marked as exhibits 1 and 2. On the other hand the defendants examined five witnesses including an Advocate Commissioner and submitted documents in support of their case which was marked as exhibits 'Ka' to exhibit-'Chha' series. The trial court after contested hearing dismissed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 31-10-1993.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 121 of 1993 before the District Judge, Moulvibazar. Eventually the said appeal was heard by the Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) 2nd court, Moulvibazar on transfer who upon contested hearing allowed the appeal and reversed the judgment and decreed of the trial court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-4-1996. At this juncture the defendant-Respondent-Petitioners moved this Court by filing this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay.

9. Mr Mahbub Ali, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that admittedly there is no dispute regarding title of the defendant No. 1 Ekhlas Mia. Both the parties to the suit unequivocally admitted that Ekhlas Mia was rightful owner in possession of 57 sataks of land in plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. Admitting indefeasible title in the property the plaintiff by sale deed No. 3481 dated 17-5-1983 purchased 26 sataks of land from Ekhlas Mia, the defendant No. 1 in suit and possession was delivered to him. Accordingly, he has been possessing the same since his purchase in the year 1993. Mr Mahbub Ali further submits that it is also not disputed that after selling 26 sataks of land to the plaintiff the defendant No. 1 Ekhlas Mia was in possession and enjoyment on the remaining 31 sataks of land which was his homestead in a compact block. Said Ekhlas Mia while in possession and enjoyment of 31 sataks land by sale deed No. 2609 dated 1-6-1991 sold out .24 sataks of land covered by plot Nos. 1362 and 1363 to defendant No. 2, Md Ali. Again by a sale deed No. 2610 dated 3-6-1991 Ekhlas Mia transferred 7 sataks of land in plot Nos. 1362 and 1363 to the defendant No. 2. Thus Ekhlas Mia sold entire land in the said two plots. The defendant No. 2 after purchase got delivery of possession of the property with definite boundary as given in the sale deed and accordingly, he has been possessing the same with the knowledge of all. He further submits that the story of dispossession of the plaintiff is false and concocted as the plaintiff in the earlier Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 filed against the defendant for permanent injunction did not even utter a single word that the defendant No. 1 has been possessing the suit land as permissive possessor under the plaintiff or the defendant No. 2.

10. He also argued that the plaintiff when could understand that he being out of possession the suit for injunction must fail then he has withdrawn the said suit with permission to sue a fresh and subsequently filed the instant suit making a story of premissive possessor seeking recovery of possession of the suit property. In fact the plaintiff never possessed the suit land. The property so far sold to him by deed of the year 1983 is totally separate and different from the land possessed and transferred to defendant No. 2. Mr Ali further submits that admittedly plaintiff and the defendants are co-sharers in two plots and there is no partition by metes and bounds among them. As such, the proper and appropriate relief for the plaintiff is to file a suit for partition praying saham of his share in the suit land. But the plaintiff filed the instant suit for recovery of possession against a co-sharer of the property which is not maintainable at all. Referring schedule to the sale deed dated 17-5-1983 exhibit-1, Mr Mahbub Ali submits that the property sold to the plaintiff is not specific and the schedule as described shows that the plaintiff purchased the property from defendant No. 1 only from plot No. 1362 and the possession of the property purchased by the plaintiff as not being described by giving definite boundary with specific possession the plaintiff cannot say that he has been dispossessed by the defendant.

11. It is also argued that the trial court while dismissing the suit rightly observed that schedule to the deed of the plaintiff is unspecific and the witnesses examined on behalf of the plaintiff could not prove exclusive possession and dispossession by the defendants. But the appellate court while allowing the appeal and decreeing the suit wrongly found that Ekhlas Mia is the owner of only 49 sataks of land covered by plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. The appellate court also wrongly found that Ekhlas Mia by sale deed dated 7-6-1983 acquired 7 sataks of land from plot No. 1359 not from plot Nos. 1362 and 1363 and as such, Ekhlas Mia cannot transfer 31 sataks of land claiming to be owner of the same to defendant No. 2. By filing an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure the petitioner prayed for accepting the sale deed dated 7-6-1983 and deed No. 2601 dated 1-6-1991 as additional evidence and to mark the same as exhibits. It is also submitted that since the deed dated 7-6-1983 has already been taken into consideration by the appellate court and observed that the said deed is in respect of plot No. 1359 only, the deed of rectification dated 1-6-1991 filed by a supplementary affidavit as annexure-'A', may be considered and marked as exhibits which left due consideration of the appellate court for better appreciation of the case and to ensure justice.

12. Finally, Mr Mahbub Ali argued that should the appellate court below consider the aforesaid two documents in conjunction with other sale deeds the appellate court below ought not to have allowed the appeal and decreed the suit because by the aforesaid two deeds it is clear that Ekhlas Mia acquired 57 sataks of land in plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. The appellate court considered title of Ekhlas Mia in respect of only 49 sataks which lead the appellate court below into an erroneous finding and on that finding allowed the appeal finding that defendant No. 1 had no title in 31 sataks of land transferred to the defendant No. 2.

13. Heard the learned Advocate for the opposite parties, have gone through the revisional application, impugned judgment and decree of both the courts below, evidences available in lower court records both oral and documentary and the document filed by a supplementary affidavit as annexure-'A'.

14. From perusal of plaint and written statement it appears that both the parties admitted that Ekhlas Mia is the owner of 57 sataks of land covered by plot Nos. 1362 and 1363. Admitting his title the plaintiff purchased 26 sataks of land from him from the said plots in question. In the plaint the plaintiff clearly stated that after his purchase defendant No. 1 Ekhlas Mia had 31 sataks of land and he was in possession of the same. It is not the case of the plaintiff that he did not get possession of the property purchased and Ekhlas Mia had no possession in the remaining 31 sataks of land covered by said two plots. The case of the plaintiff is that the defendant No. 1 requested him to permit him to live in the suit house for the time being to enable him to construct his house on the property adjacent to the plaintiff's property. The defendant No. 1 Ekhlas Mia while in possession of the schedule-2 suit house the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 against the defendant No. 2 and others for a decree of permanent injunction. Now here in the said plaint in Title Suit No. 33 of 1991 the plaintiff claimed that the suit property is in possession of defendant No. 1 as permissive possessor. But the plaintiff clearly stated that he is in possession and the defendant No. 2 in the present suit along with his gangmen threatened the plaintiff with dispossession on 23rd Jaistha 1398 BS and in the said suit the plaintiff claimed that the defendant No. 2 of this suit purchased the land just adjacent to his land and trying to dispossess the plaintiff declaring that he will construct pucca building on the suit land.

15. Subsequently, the said suit was withdrawn on the ground of formal defect with permission to sue a fresh and then filed the instant suit for recovery of possession. From the pleadings of the party and the evidences adduced, it appears that the property in question is an undivided one. Both the parties are co-sharer in the suit land. There was no partition by metes and bound. In such a situation if a co-sharer of the property thinks that he has been deprived of his share by other co-sharer may ventilate his grievance by filing a partition suit seeking saham of his share and get the property partitioned through court and delivery of possession of the same but a suit for mere recovery of possession is not maintainable without determination of their share in the property. From evidences both oral and documentary it is not clear in which portion of the two plots the possession was delivered to the plaintiff.

16. Moreover, from the schedule to the sale deed, exhibit-1 it is difficult to find that possession in which portion of the suit plot was delivered to the plaintiff. In such a situation without a suit for partition a suit for recovery of possession is not at all maintainable. The trial court upon consideration of the evidences on record rightly found that Ekhlas Mia is the owner of 57 sataks land. He transferred 26 sataks to the plaintiff and the remaining 31 sataks of land to the defendant No. 2. The trial court also observed that there is no evidence to be believed that the plaintiff was dispossessed from the suit land but it is the clear admission of the plaintiff that the defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit land though he claims that he has given permission to the Defendant No. 1 to live therein.

<u>17. The plaintiff as PW 1 deposed in respect of possession and dispossession, no other witnesses supported his claim that he was in possession and he has been dispossessed by the defendants. In a suit for recovery of possession the plaintiff is to prove his possession at first and then his dispossession by the defendant by evidence. But in the present suit nobody came forward to depose that the plaintiff was dispossessed on such and such date or the plaintiff had been in possession of the suit land since his purchase and he permitted the defendant No. 1 to live in the suit house for the time being. In the absence of such assertion or evidences possession and dispossession of the plaintiff in the suit land is not established.</u>

18. Moreover, in the earlier suit the plaintiff did not make such story that he has been possessing the suit land through defendant No. 1 as permissive possessor. No evidence adduced on behalf of the plaintiff to establish his case in whose presence the defendant No. 1 was allowed to reside in the suit house. Mere testimony and claim of the plaintiff alone cannot ipso facto prove that he allowed the defendant No. 1 to reside in the suit house as permissive possessor or before that he had been possessing the same and dispossessed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2.

19. It is also not the case of the plaintiff that defendant No. 1 refrained himself from surrendering possession of the suit house to the plaintiff denying title of the plaintiff or claiming title in the property. But a case has been made out to the effect that taking advantage of possession of the defendant No.1 in the suit house the defendant No. 2 with his gangmen dispossessed the plaintiff. The trial court while dismissing the suit found that the plaintiff could not prove exclusive possession of the suit property before alleged date of dispossession and also could not prove in what manner and on what time the defendant No. 2 dispossessed the plaintiff.

20. I have gone through the judgment of the appellate court. From perusal of the same this Court finds that the appellate court while allowing the appeal mainly considered the fact that Ekhlas Mia did not acquire 57 sataks of land in two suit plots by considering a deed dated 7-6-1983 by which he purchased 7 sataks of land. The said deed shows that Ekhlas Mia purchased 7 sataks of land from plot No. 1359, but subsequently, by a deed of the year 1991 annexure-'A' to the supplementary affidavit the deed dated 7-6-1983 has been rectified by the vendor wherein plot No. 1362 has been inserted by the rectification deed dated 1-6-1991. It is established that Ekhlas Mia purchased 7 sataks of land from plot No. 1362 not from plot No. 1359. The deed dated 7-6-1983 has not been marked as exhibit before the trial court, but the appellate court has taken the same into consideration and considering the said deed came to a finding that in the absence of title of the Ekhlas Mia in 31 sataks of land he cannot transfer the same to defendant No. 2 and the Defendant 2 cannot claim 31 sataks in the two suit plots. Had the rectification deed dated 1-6-1991 been placed before the appellate court and considered it in conjunction with the deed dated 7-6-1983, the lower appellate court would not have allowed the appeal and decreed the suit. Since the appellate court considered the deed dated 7-6-1983 in its judgment this court thinks that it would be just and expedient to consider the deed of rectification dated 1-6-1991 submitted before this Court by supplementary affidavit as annexure-'A' in conjunction with the deed dated 7-6-1983 for ends of justice. Accordingly, for proper adjudication of the dispute before this Court I am inclined to allow the application and mark those documents as 'X' and 'Y' respectively. Apart from this where both the parties admitted that Ekhlas Mia is the owner of 57 sataks of land in two plots the appellate court should not have made out a 3rd case beyond pleadings and evidences on record. In such a situation both the documents of the year 1983 and 1991 have been considered to come into a definite finding that there cannot be any question at all that Ekhlas Mia is not the owner of 57 sataks of land.

21. In the instant suit since the plaintiff failed to prove his possession and dispossession by evidence the trial court rightly dismissed the suit. But the appellate court instead of considering evidences on record piecemeally considering a deed of the year, 1983 (Mark-"X") and allowed the appeal and as such, has committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice.

22. Taking into consideration of the above, this Court finds merit in the Rule as well as in the submissions of the petitioners counsel calling interference by this Court.

23. In the result, the Rule is made absolute.

24. The judgment and decree dated 18-4-1996 passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge), 2nd Court, Moulvibazar, in Title Appeal No. 121 of 1993 is hereby set side and the judgment and decree dated 31-10-1993 passed by the trial court in Title Suit No. 46 of 1991 is restored.

25. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacate.

26. There will be no order as to costs.

Communicate a copy of this judgment and send down the lower court records to the court concerned at once.

End.
